rows.note: Use this as the everyday noun phrase for a large, usually tangible quantity; it is the all-purpose choice among the quantity renderings here.

example.english: There are a lot of documents on the table, so help me sort them out.
example.traditional: 枱面有一大堆文件，快啲幫我整理吓。
example.jyutping: toi2 min6 jau5 jat1 daai6 deoi1 man4 gin6 faai3 di1 bong1 ngo5 zing2 lei5 haa5

rows.note: Use this when “the whole lot” means all the members of a set or everything.

example.english: We need to take the whole lot in this box with us.
example.traditional: 呢盒嘢我哋要全部帶走。
example.jyutping: nei1 hap6 je5 ngo5 dei6 jiu3 cyun4 bou6 daai3 zau2

rows.note: Use this specifically for a distinct parcel of land, especially a building or development site.

example.english: The price of this lot of land has gone up a lot.
example.traditional: 呢幅地皮個價升咗好多。
example.jyutping: nei1 fuk1 dei6 pei4 go3 gaa3 sing1 zo2 hou2 do1

rows.note: Use this for a group of people considered collectively, including a group being described critically.

example.english: That lot of people are making noise downstairs again.
example.traditional: 嗰一班人又喺樓下嘈喇。
example.jyutping: go2 jat1 baan1 jan4 jau6 hai2 lau4 haa6 cou4 laa3
